title: ring144_24v, stride layout
claim: the study's starting point: the rotation pass laying riders out by stride, recompiled on 2026-10-20 with a compiler that keeps every qubit's gates in order: 824 batches of 1.05 contacts each, which is why it takes 1.42 s. The study's 546 batches and 520 ms came from a compiler that reordered a qubit's gates, which the checker now refuses.

marks.label: rigid rotation
marks.note: one loop_shift template turns the whole loop: every rider moves with one waveform, 144 ions here. This is the broadcast primitive the ring is built around. Every loaded site the rotation does not move -- a docked ancilla -- HOLDS meanwhile: its two-way switch selects the hold bank instead of the motion bank, 1 select bit per site per cycle. A switchless channel cannot hold a docked ion while it moves the loop (R4d).

marks.label: batch 1 of 824 / a 1-contact batch (786 of 824)
marks.note: a dock: 1 riders pull into their spurs at once. Each batch pays dock + undock + one forced cool (about 725 us) whatever its size; mean fill here is 1.0 contacts of 3 possible.  ALSO: one rider docks alone, and the batch still pays its full overhead: 786 such batches cost about 573.8 ms for 91.0% of the contacts.

marks.label: forced cool
marks.note: 300 us, once per batch: an ion that has crossed a junction carries 3 quanta against a 1-quantum gate budget, so the cool is structural, not a policy. Cooling is 17% of the round.

marks.label: contact gates (1 pairs at once)
marks.note: the two-qubit gates of one batch, all in one instruction; each pair sits in its own dock. The Circuit pane shows which QASM statements this discharges.

marks.label: undock
marks.note: the riders leave their spurs. Entering the degree-3 rail node is charged as a junction crossing -- the price of the only mechanism a loop has.

marks.label: the fullest batch (3 contacts)
marks.note: every ancilla in use at once: this is what the lockstep placement is engineered to make happen, and the per-batch overhead is amortised best here.

numbers.r10_verdict: -> R10 passed: O1 by the proved Lean checker (QCCDC.Cert.check_sound); O2 by stabilizer tableau, composed from the emitted pulses, against the source QASM

title: ring(143, 3, 36), 288 slots, 36 ancillas, per-site switches -- the recommended design
claim: 46 batches, 341 hops, 55.6 ms, R10 passed: the proved Lean checker and the tableau. Its rotation schedule is within 10.7% of its lower bound; its batches are 52% full. It has per-site two-way switches, the deck's: each site follows the motion bank or the hold bank of the 32 broadcast channels, so it pays 1 select bit per site per transport cycle. The switchless declaration it was compiled for was dropped on 2026-10-23: R4d's hold clause refuses it, because a switchless channel cannot hold a docked ion while it moves the loop. That is 324 select bits a cycle, 64.8 Mbit/s at the 5 us rotation step; the 32 broadcast DACs are exactly the motion bank and the hold bank (58 with the shims). The shims cost time: 17.1 ms a round through the 1:100 demultiplexer (WISE, once per reconfiguration), 2.7 ms at 1:16 with 162 shim DACs. Not buildable by today's DRC: 150 of 324 sites are short of 3 control-electrode pairs (the 36 docks, the 36 rail sites they hang off, and 78 more).

title: grid13x13, 312 traps, direct wiring and direct control
claim: a real direct machine: grid13x13 with control.model 'direct', so a cycle may play several waveforms. It does in most: 930 of 1,319 transport cycles move ions in two to eight directions at once (up to 10 distinct motions, 11 waveforms with the hold), and the round takes 405.6 ms at 4.8 ions per instruction -- against 866.1 ms for the same lattice told to play one waveform a cycle (12). Every site has channels of its own: no select bits, and 12,480 DACs, over the task's 128.

marks.label: cool
marks.note: the lattice cools too; 7% of its round.

marks.label: 8 directions at once
marks.note: ions moving 8 different ways in one instruction. A ring rotation asks for one. Every site of a direct machine has channels of its own, so this is legal here. The 32-channel broadcast block is two banks of 16, a motion and the hold, so it plays one of these per cycle: R4d counts the banks, R22 the cycles.
